title: Evaluation of postmortem endomyocardial biopsy specimens from 38 patients with lymphocytic myocarditis: implications for role of sampling error
study_context: Postmortem simulated endomyocardial sampling of 38 hearts with lymphocytic myocarditis contributing to death.
population_or_data: Postmortem simulated endomyocardial sampling of 38 hearts with lymphocytic myocarditis contributing to death.
task: Postmortem simulated endomyocardial sampling of 38 hearts with lymphocytic myocarditis contributing to death.
method: Comparison of ten biopsy-sized samples per ventricle with larger ventricular myocardial slices using Dallas criteria.
main_findings: In hearts known to have lymphocytic myocarditis at autopsy, biopsy-sized specimens frequently missed diagnostic inflammation, illustrating spatial sampling error even when multiple specimens were examined.
limitations: Abstract-only review. PDF pages 1 and extracted text visually checked on 2026-10-07.

Myocarditis is not transplant rejection; no modern ACR sensitivity estimate follows. Postmortem simulated biopsies are not independent clinical biopsy validation and a whole-heart diagnosis cannot label every crop as positive.
does_not_establish: Myocarditis is not transplant rejection; no modern ACR sensitivity estimate follows. Postmortem simulated biopsies are not independent clinical biopsy validation and a whole-heart diagnosis cannot label every crop as positive.
relevance_to_project: A rationale for distinguishing disease in the whole heart from visible diagnostic lesions in a sampled biopsy or cropped region.
